validated_results.title: Dietary Fiber Intake and Risk of Advanced and Aggressive Forms of Prostate Cancer: A Pooled Analysis of 15 Prospective Cohort Studies.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
validated_results.reason: Prospective pooled analysis of 15 cohort studies evaluating total dietary fiber intake and incident prostate cancer risk.

sample_size.excerpt: During follow up of 842,149 men in 15 cohorts, 52,683 were diagnosed with incident PC. Among the PC cases, 4,863 were advanced tumors, 2,978 advanced restricted tumors, 3,097 PC deaths, and 9,673 high-grade tumors.

cases.excerpt: During follow up of 842,149 men in 15 cohorts, 52,683 were diagnosed with incident PC. Among the PC cases, 4,863 were advanced tumors, 2,978 advanced restricted tumors, 3,097 PC deaths, and 9,673 high-grade tumors.

confidence_interval.excerpt: lowest quintile=0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.76–0.93), advanced restricted PC (MVHR=0.85, 95%CI 0.74–0.97), and PC mortality (MVHR=0.78, 95%CI 0.68–0.89); statistically significant trends were noted for each of these associations (p≤0.03), while a null association was observed for high grade PC for the same comparison (MVHR=1.00, 95%CI 0.93–1.07).

design.excerpt: Pooled analysis of the primary data in 15 cohorts in three continents.

timing.excerpt: 842,149 men were followed for up to 9–22 years between 1985–2009 across studies.

continent.excerpt: These analyses were conducted using data from 15 cohort studies from North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia
continent.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS - Study Population, paragraph 1

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Baseline dietary fiber intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire or diet history in each study.
